title: CSS Source and Build Boundaries
hints: Treat Build/Sources/Sass/ as the source of truth when a Sass source exists.
Do not hand-edit generated public CSS as the only change.
Verify generated assets are in sync when public assets are committed.
Use lintScss for TYPO3's stylelint setup and npm -- run build-css for a focused CSS build while iterating.

title: CSS Component Structure
hints: Prefer focused component partials in the existing Sass structure.
Keep selectors close to the owning UI component.
Use forms, scaffold, dashboard, and element folders for their owning concerns instead of creating broad global styles.

title: CSS Browser Target
hints: TYPO3 backend CSS targets evergreen browsers as they exist on the day of the corresponding TYPO3 LTS release.
Modern CSS features are acceptable when they fit the active LTS evergreen browser target and the build pipeline accepts them.
CSS features may be adopted before the LTS release when they are expected to be part of the evergreen browser baseline at LTS release time.
Early adoption must be intentional, reviewable, and limited to features with a clear path into the LTS browser baseline.
When CSS changes are backported to older TYPO3 versions, the CSS must fully match the evergreen browser baseline of that target release year.
Do not backport CSS features that only match a newer release baseline unless the target branch already supports them.
Avoid compatibility workarounds for obsolete browsers outside the active LTS browser target.
Prefer native CSS capabilities over JavaScript workarounds when the feature is supported by the LTS target.
The Popover API is an example where native platform behavior should be preferred over custom JavaScript positioning or visibility logic when the target baseline supports it.

title: Minimal CSS and Reusable Components
hints: Write as little new CSS as possible.
Prefer reusing, extending, or composing existing TYPO3 backend components before adding new CSS.
New CSS should express reusable component behavior, not one-off page-specific tweaks.
Utility classes should be used only in exceptional cases and must not replace a missing reusable component.

title: CSS Class Naming
hints: Use existing component naming conventions from nearby Sass files.
TYPO3 backend component classes usually use a short component root plus hyphenated elements or variants, for example .panel-heading, .toolbar-item, or .module-docheader.
Variants should customize the base component through custom properties whenever possible.
Do not introduce a new naming system such as BEM-style block__element--modifier unless the surrounding component already uses it.
Use t3js-* classes only as JavaScript hooks and keep them separate from visual styling selectors.

title: Styleguide Demos for CSS Components
hints: All CSS components must be represented with demos in the styleguide extension.
New CSS components need a matching styleguide demo.
Changed CSS components should update an existing styleguide demo or add one when no demo exists.
Backend component demos usually live below typo3/sysext/styleguide/Resources/Private/Templates/Backend/Components/.

title: CSS Tokens and Specificity
hints: Prefer existing --typo3-* custom properties for TYPO3 backend colors, spacing, borders, shadows, transitions, and state styles.
Use component-local custom properties to map component concepts to global TYPO3 tokens.
Expose a small, named component property contract when variants, host context, or states need to tune the component.
Keep specificity low and predictable.
Avoid !important unless overriding external or unavoidable generated styles.

title: Web Components and Element Styles
hints: Styles for TYPO3 custom elements should start at the custom element host selector.
Keep custom element Sass below Build/Sources/Sass/element/ when the style belongs to a web component.
Use CSS custom properties, ::part(...), slots, and explicit host attributes as stable styling boundaries.
Do not style arbitrary internal DOM depth when a host selector, part, slot, or custom property can express the contract.

title: State Attributes and Semantic Selectors
hints: Prefer semantic attributes and explicit state APIs over ad hoc visual classes for component state.
ARIA attributes must reflect real accessibility state and must not be introduced only as CSS hooks.
State selectors should map to component properties whenever possible.
Keep JavaScript, markup, CSS, and tests in sync when a state attribute changes.

hints.text: Do not use --token-color-* values directly in component CSS; they define the color space for semantic tokens.
Use --typo3-text-color-* for text and icons, --typo3-surface-* for larger backgrounds, and --typo3-surface-container-* for nested component backgrounds.
Surface tokens may be used directly, but they must follow the logical layering order: lowest, low, base, high, highest.
Use matching *-text surface tokens when placing content on stateful surfaces.
Use --typo3-state-* tokens for interactive or semantic states and derive subtle borders with color-mix(...) plus --typo3-border-mix.

There is no semantic surface, text-color or state layer here. The backend's custom properties are component-scoped — --typo3-component-bg, --typo3-component-color, --typo3-component-border-color, the --typo3-input-* family — and below them sit the Bootstrap variables the backend still builds on.

title: Shadow Tokens and Layering

hints.text: Shadows must follow the same logical layering model as surfaces.

hints: Prefer semantic shadow tokens over raw box-shadow values.

hints.text: Use stronger shadows only for higher layers such as flyouts, dialogs, popovers, tooltips, overlays, and windows.
Keep surface elevation and shadow strength aligned.

title: Z-Index and Overlay Layering

hints.text: Prefer existing z-index tokens such as --typo3-zindex-dropdown, --typo3-zindex-modal-backdrop, --typo3-zindex-modal, and --typo3-zindex-header.

hints: Place overlays, flyouts, menus, sticky headers, dialogs, and popovers deliberately in the backend layering model.
Avoid raw z-index numbers when an existing token matches the intended layer.
Do not use extremely high z-index values to win stacking conflicts; fix the owning stacking context or use the correct layer token.
Keep z-index, shadow strength, and surface elevation aligned.

title: Motion and Transitions

hints.text: Prefer existing transition tokens such as --typo3-transition-color for interactive color, border, shadow, and opacity transitions.

hints: New transitions or animations that move, resize, fade large regions, or affect focus/navigation must respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
Avoid transition: all unless the surrounding component already uses it and the affected properties are intentionally constrained.
Keep motion functional and subtle so it clarifies state changes.

title: Container Queries and Responsive Components
hints: Prefer component-local responsiveness over viewport-only breakpoints when a component can appear in different backend containers.
Use container-type: inline-size and container queries for reusable components when layout depends on available container width.
Container queries are an example of a modern CSS feature that may be introduced before an LTS release when they are expected to be part of the LTS browser baseline.
Keep container query rules scoped to the owning component.
Do not add global breakpoints for a component-specific layout problem unless the behavior is truly tied to the viewport or scaffold.

title: Light and Dark Mode CSS
hints: CSS changes must work in both light and dark backend color schemes.

hints.text: Prefer semantic TYPO3 custom properties such as surfaces, text colors, component colors, input colors, and state colors.
Use existing light-dark(...) patterns when a value genuinely needs distinct light and dark variants.

hints: Check contrast for text, icons, borders, focus outlines, and state backgrounds in both schemes.

title: RTL and Logical CSS Properties
hints: All backend components must be checked for RTL support.
Prefer logical properties such as margin-inline, padding-inline, inset-inline, and border-inline over physical left/right properties.
Use TYPO3 position custom properties such as --typo3-position-start, --typo3-position-end, and --typo3-position-modifier for direction-aware calculations.
Direction-aware transforms, icons, carets, flyouts, drag handles, resize handles, trees, lists, tables, toolbars, and form controls need explicit RTL review.

title: Bootstrap Transition in Backend CSS
hints: TYPO3 still uses Bootstrap CSS in parts of the backend, but Bootstrap usage is being actively reduced.
Treat Bootstrap as existing infrastructure, not as the preferred target architecture for new TYPO3-specific UI.
Avoid introducing new high-specificity Bootstrap overrides; prefer TYPO3 component styles for TYPO3-specific behavior.

title: CSS Accessibility, Contrast, and States
hints: Color contrast must satisfy WCAG requirements in both light and dark color schemes.
Interactive elements must be reachable and operable by keyboard.
Keyboard focus must be visible with :focus-visible or an equivalent pattern.
Focus order must remain logical, and intentional focus traps need a safe escape path.
Hoverable interactive elements must have hover styles.
Check hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, empty, error, selected, expanded, and collapsed states when applicable.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate state.
Interactive icon-only controls need an accessible name, while decorative icons should be hidden from assistive technology.

title: Icons, Text, and Layout Stability
hints: Components that combine icons, labels, badges, carets, and actions must keep layout stable across hover, focus, active, loading, and disabled states.
Use logical spacing for icon and text gaps, for example margin-inline-* or gap, so RTL layouts remain correct.
Define overflow behavior for long labels in compact backend UI.
Hover and focus styles must not cause avoidable layout shifts.
